title: Plans, weather and leisure
objectives: I can talk about future plans with ir plus an infinitive.
I can describe the weather and name the seasons.
I can invite someone, and accept or decline an invitation politely.
I can use poder, querer, saber, precisar and dever with an infinitive and talk about hobbies.

vocabulary.note: Context tells you whether it means weather or time.

It is sunny today.
The rain starts in the afternoon.
It is very windy today.
The sky is cloudy.

vocabulary.note: In speech people say both faz calor and está calor.

example.en: It is very hot in the summer.
It is cold in winter.

vocabulary.note: In Brazil summer runs from December to March.

example.en: In summer we go to the beach.

example.pt: Eu vou à academia de manhã.
example.en: I go to the gym in the morning.

example.pt: Que tal cinema hoje à noite?

vocabulary.en: to play a game or sport

example.en: Today I can't go.

example.en: Do you know how to play soccer?

vocabulary.note: With a noun it needs de: preciso de ajuda. With a verb there is no de: preciso estudar.

dialogues.title: Planos para o fim de semana
dialogues.context: Beatriz and her friend Thiago talk about what they are going to do this weekend.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Oi, Thiago! O que você vai fazer no fim de semana?
lines.en: Hi, Thiago! What are you going to do on the weekend?

lines.speaker: Thiago
lines.pt: No sábado eu vou jogar futebol com os amigos. E você?
lines.en: On Saturday I'm going to play soccer with friends. And you?

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Eu vou ficar em casa. Preciso estudar.
lines.en: I'm going to stay home. I need to study.

lines.speaker: Thiago
lines.pt: No domingo a gente vai fazer um churrasco. Você topa?
lines.en: On Sunday we're going to have a barbecue. Are you up for it?

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Com certeza! Que horas?
lines.en: Of course! What time?

lines.speaker: Thiago
lines.pt: Por volta da uma hora.
lines.en: Around one o'clock.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Posso levar alguma coisa?
lines.en: Can I bring something?

lines.speaker: Thiago
lines.pt: Pode levar um refrigerante.
lines.en: You can bring a soft drink.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Combinado. Vai ter sol?
lines.en: Deal. Will it be sunny?

lines.speaker: Thiago
lines.pt: Vai! Vai fazer calor.
lines.en: Yes! It's going to be hot.

dialogues.title: Vamos à praia?
dialogues.context: Camila, Diego and Larissa are friends in Rio de Janeiro. Camila wants to go to the beach.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Gente, vamos à praia amanhã?
lines.en: Guys, shall we go to the beach tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Amanhã eu não posso. Preciso trabalhar. Que tal no domingo?
lines.en: I can't tomorrow. I need to work. How about Sunday?

lines.speaker: Larissa
lines.pt: Domingo eu posso. Mas vai fazer calor ou vai chover?
lines.en: I can on Sunday. But will it be hot or is it going to rain?

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Olha no celular: domingo tem sol e faz trinta graus.
lines.en: Look on my phone: Sunday is sunny and thirty degrees.

lines.speaker: Larissa
lines.pt: Perfeito! Eu vou levar o protetor solar.
lines.en: Perfect! I'm going to bring the sunscreen.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Eu não sei nadar bem, mas gosto da praia.
lines.en: I don't swim well, but I like the beach.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Sem problema! A gente vai de ônibus?
lines.en: No problem! Are we going by bus?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Vamos de ônibus, eu não tenho carro.
lines.en: Let's go by bus, I don't have a car.

lines.speaker: Larissa
lines.pt: Então a gente se encontra no ponto às oito.
lines.en: Then we meet at the bus stop at eight.

dialogues.title: Que pena!
dialogues.context: Ana invites her coworker Rui to the movies, but he has a problem.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Rui, você quer ir ao cinema hoje à noite?
lines.en: Rui, do you want to go to the movies tonight?

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Hoje eu não posso. Preciso trabalhar até tarde.
lines.en: I can't today. I need to work late.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Que pena! E amanhã?
lines.en: What a pity! And tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Amanhã sim. Que filme você quer ver?
lines.en: Tomorrow, yes. What movie do you want to see?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Uma comédia. Vamos às sete?
lines.en: A comedy. Shall we go at seven?

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Às sete está ótimo. Mas amanhã vai chover.
lines.en: Seven is great. But it's going to rain tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Sem problema. O cinema fica no shopping.
lines.en: No problem. The movie theater is in the mall.

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Verdade! Então combinado. A gente se encontra lá.
lines.en: True! Then it's a deal. We'll meet there.

grammar.title: The near future: ir plus infinitive
grammar.explanation:
The usual way to talk about the future in everyday Brazilian Portuguese is ir in the present followed by an infinitive, just like going to in English: eu vou viajar amanhã, I'm going to travel tomorrow. Conjugate ir and leave the second verb in the infinitive: eu vou estudar, você vai estudar, nós vamos estudar, vocês vão estudar.

For the negative, put não before ir: eu não vou viajar. For questions, use the same order or just raise your voice: você vai viajar? O que você vai fazer amanhã? To say there will be something, use vai ter: vai ter chuva, vai ter festa.

Time expressions go at the beginning or end of the sentence: amanhã, hoje à noite, no sábado, no fim de semana, semana que vem, mês que vem, no ano que vem. With a verb of motion, you can simply use the present of ir: eu vou à praia amanhã. In fast speech vou often sounds like vô, but it is always written vou.

examples.pt: Amanhã eu vou ficar em casa.
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm going to stay home.

examples.pt: O que você vai fazer no fim de semana?
examples.en: What are you going to do on the weekend?

examples.pt: A gente vai fazer um churrasco no domingo.
examples.en: We are going to have a barbecue on Sunday.

examples.pt: Eles não vão viajar em julho.
examples.en: They are not going to travel in July.

examples.pt: Vai ter chuva à tarde.
examples.en: There is going to be rain in the afternoon.

grammar.title: Poder, querer, saber, precisar, dever
grammar.explanation:
These verbs are followed directly by an infinitive, with no preposition: eu posso ir, eu quero sair, eu sei nadar, eu preciso estudar, eu devo descansar. The first three are irregular. Poder: posso, pode, podemos, podem. Querer: quero, quer, queremos, querem. Saber: sei, sabe, sabemos, sabem. Dever: devo, deve, devemos, devem. Precisar is regular: preciso, precisa, precisamos, precisam.

Meanings matter. Poder means can or may, for ability, possibility or permission: posso entrar? Saber means to know how to, for a learned skill: eu sei nadar, I know how to swim. Eu posso nadar means that nothing stops me from swimming today. Querer is to want and precisar is to need. Precisar takes de before a noun: preciso de ajuda. Dever usually means should: você deve descansar.

In casual speech, Brazilians often use ter que (or tem que) instead of dever or precisar for obligations: eu tenho que trabalhar amanhã. Use pode to request politely: você pode me ajudar? And queria is softer than quero: eu queria um café.

examples.pt: Hoje eu não posso ir à festa.
examples.en: Today I can't go to the party.

examples.pt: Eu quero viajar em julho.
examples.en: I want to travel in July.

examples.pt: Você sabe nadar?
examples.en: Do you know how to swim?

examples.pt: Nós precisamos sair cedo.
examples.en: We need to leave early.

examples.pt: Você deve descansar no fim de semana.
examples.en: You should rest on the weekend.

grammar.title: Weather and seasons
grammar.explanation:
Portuguese uses different verbs for the weather. Faz is used for temperature and sun: faz calor, faz frio, faz sol. Tem is used for things that exist in the sky: tem sol, tem vento, tem nuvens. Está is used for how things are right now: está nublado, está quente, está frio. For rain, say está chovendo, it is raining, or vai chover, it is going to rain. The verb chover has no eu or você form, only chove.

In everyday speech Brazilians also say está calor and está frio in place of faz calor and faz frio. Both are fine. To ask about the weather, use como está o tempo? or que tempo faz? To state a temperature, use faz plus the number plus graus: faz trinta graus. The word muito is used before the noun in these expressions: faz muito calor, não faz muito frio.

The seasons are o verão (summer), o outono (autumn), o inverno (winter) and a primavera (spring). Brazil is in the Southern Hemisphere, so the seasons are the reverse of those in North America and Europe: summer is from December to March and winter is from June to September.

examples.pt: Hoje faz muito calor no Rio.
examples.en: Today it is very hot in Rio.

examples.pt: Em julho faz frio em Porto Alegre.
examples.en: In July it is cold in Porto Alegre.

examples.pt: Hoje tem sol, mas amanhã vai chover.
examples.en: Today is sunny, but tomorrow it is going to rain.

examples.pt: Está chovendo e o céu está nublado.
examples.en: It is raining and the sky is cloudy.

examples.pt: Faz trinta graus na praia.
examples.en: It is thirty degrees at the beach.

grammar.title: Invitations: inviting, accepting and declining
grammar.explanation:
The most natural way to invite someone is vamos plus a place or an infinitive: vamos à praia? vamos ver um filme? You can also use que tal plus a noun or an infinitive: que tal um churrasco? que tal viajar no fim de semana? The direct question você quer...? and the informal você topa? (are you up for it?) are also common.

To accept, say claro, com certeza, topo, boa ideia or combinado. To decline politely, give a reason and show that you are sorry: hoje eu não posso, preciso trabalhar; que pena, mas eu não posso; fica para outra vez (let's do it another time). A simple não, with no reason, can sound rude in Brazil, so a short explanation is normal.

To agree on time and place, use a que horas? and onde?, then confirm with combinado or fechado. Brazilians often say a gente se encontra... (we meet...) for arrangements: a gente se encontra no ponto às oito.

rows: Shall we go to the beach?
Hoje eu não posso. Que pena!
I can't today. What a pity!

examples.pt: Vamos ao cinema hoje à noite?
examples.en: Shall we go to the movies tonight?

examples.pt: Que tal jogar futebol no sábado?
examples.en: How about playing soccer on Saturday?

examples.pt: Eu topo! A que horas?
examples.en: I'm up for it! At what time?

examples.pt: Hoje não posso, preciso estudar.
examples.en: I can't today, I need to study.

examples.pt: A gente se encontra às oito, combinado?
examples.en: We'll meet at eight, deal?

culture.title: Weekends, weather and plans
culture.text:
Weekends in Brazil often revolve around friends and family. The classic plan is a churrasco, a barbecue with grilled meat, farofa and cold drinks, usually on Sunday at someone's house. Soccer is everywhere: people play a casual game called pelada with friends, and watch their favorite team on TV. In coastal cities the praia is a weekend habit, and in Rio de Janeiro you will see people on the sand all year long.

Because Brazil is in the Southern Hemisphere, summer is from December to March and winter is from June to September. Most of the country is warm all year, but the South can be cold, with frost and even snow on a few mountain days in July. The hot, rainy season in much of the country is the summer, when heavy afternoon storms are common. Carnaval happens in February or early March, in the hottest months, and festas juninas take place in June, in winter.

When Brazilians say vamos marcar or a gente combina, it does not always mean that a plan is fixed. If you want to be sure, propose a day and a time and wait for a combinado. Declining an invitation is normal, but it is friendlier to give a reason and suggest another day.
